title: Compute 'what to do next' in athena strategy from map and roadmap
summary: Add a computed next-steps section to `athena strategy`: read each roadmap step's Rows list, look up those rows' statuses in the requirements map, drop steps with no open rows, and print the rest in roadmap order with open rows and counts. Replace the hand-written 'What to do next' list in strategy-view.md with a pointer to the command, and add a test that fails if that list returns or the roadmap and map disagree. The audience is the user and a cold reader who need a current next-steps list.

defaults_applied.how: Unit tests plus a real-file test; cargo test and clippy criteria.
Criteria run `athena strategy` and check the output changes with map status.
Compute the list from state instead of refreshing the text.
Behavior criteria use cargo run/test the verifier can run.
Implemented in the existing Rust CLI module.
One focused change in the strategy module and its doc.
Docs and decision note written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: 'Athena's own state' means the requirements map statuses plus the roadmap's per-step Rows lists, both already in the repo; no new record type is introduced.

Order comes from the roadmap's step order (file order). The 'course correction to outcomes' is a priority judgment I cannot find computed anywhere; if the roadmap's prose still puts acceleration first, reordering roadmap.md is a hand edit and is only done if the producer can find the corrected order in the repo.
The hand-written 'Blocked by' prose is dropped from the view; the roadmap's own 'What' and 'Done when' remain the place for it.
Only strategy.rs's existing parsing style (markdown tables and bullet lists) is reused; no new crate.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo run -q -p athena-cli -- strategy` (binary name may differ; use the athena-cli package) from the repo root: after the per-goal coverage it prints a next-steps section listing each roadmap step (RM-n) that still has partial or not-covered rows, with its open row IDs and counts, taken from the map and roadmap. Steps whose rows are all Covered do not appear. Exit stays 0 when sources agree.
`cargo run -q -p athena-cli -- strategy --json` includes the same next steps as structured data (step id, title, open row ids).

Unit tests in strategy.rs use small fixture map and roadmap texts to show: a step with all rows covered is dropped; flipping a row's status in the map changes the output; a map row open but in no roadmap step, a roadmap row absent from the map, and a row in two steps are each reported as errors (exit 2). `cargo test -p athena-cli` passes.

A test over the real files fails if docs/design/strategy-view.md again contains a hand-written ordered 'What to do next' list, and passes on the real map and roadmap with no errors. `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.

strategy-view.md no longer contains the numbered hand-written list; its 'What to do next' section says the steps come from `athena strategy` and the roadmap, and states where the order comes from. A reader can see that the stale items (acceleration first, built introspection listed as unbuilt) are gone.

The docs record the change: a CHANGELOG entry and a decision note giving the alternatives considered (generate the text into the doc and test for drift, versus compute on demand) and the root-cause reason.

out_of_scope: Rewriting the roadmap's priorities or the course correction itself
departures: Slightly lower acceptance: how 'next' is ordered (roadmap file order versus a derived priority) is a judgment the request leaves open.
